title: I Stopped to Think
gist_ar: مقال عن إن تغيير كلمة صغيرة بيغيّر المعنى.
text:
I remember reading that small grammatical choices change meaning more than large vocabulary ones. I did not believe it until I began teaching and had to explain why 'I stopped smoking' and 'I stopped to smoke' describe opposite lives.

English allows a verb to mean two things depending on what follows it. If you regret to tell somebody something, you are about to deliver bad news; if you regret telling them, you have already done it and wish you had not. A manager who means to reduce costs intends it; a decision that means reducing costs has that consequence. Learners who avoid noticing this can manage for years and then be misunderstood at an important moment.

What interests me is that nobody considers these pairs difficult once they stop trying to memorise them. The pattern is meaningful, not arbitrary: the infinitive looks forward to a purpose, and the gerund looks back at an action. Try remembering that instead. I would suggest not learning a list — I would suggest listening for the direction the sentence is facing.
